aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.prompt: A 22-year-old comes to a community agency “just for a housing letter.” In the same first interview she says she has not slept in three nights and that her partner tracks her phone. As the BSW completing intake, what should you do with that extra information?

options.a: Put housing, sleep, and partner tracking on today’s intake and screen safety before you close
options.b: Print the housing letter only and book a separate “clinical” visit next week for everything else
options.c: Hand her PHQ-9 and GAD-7 first and delay housing and safety talk until the scores print
options.d: Send her to an LCSW for a DSM-5-TR interview before any bachelor-level casework may start

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.explanation: Bachelor-level intake is one biopsychosocial interview, not a housing-only form. Concrete need, sleep disruption, and possible intimate-partner control are all first-session data. Screen safety in this contact; do not park risk until a later “clinical” hour or a diagnosis visit.

distractorExplanations.b: Splitting “paperwork” from “clinical” delays safety screening; the housing request is still part of today’s assessment.
distractorExplanations.c: Symptom checklists do not outrank safety or housing; they can supplement intake, not postpone it.
distractorExplanations.d: DSM differential is not the BSW gate to casework; you assess needs and safety now and refer when indicated.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.prompt: In a shelter intake a woman begins describing her partner’s threats. He is waiting in the lobby “to help with paperwork.” What is the BSW’s first assessment move?

options.a: Bring him in so you can complete a couples genogram and watch how the two of them interact
options.b: See her alone, screen current safety and privacy, and do not open with a joint session
options.c: Have him complete a collateral mental-health form in the lobby while she talks with you
options.d: Teach the cycle of violence in the waiting area so both of them hear the same lecture today

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.explanation: With intimate-partner violence, the first interview priority is privacy and a current safety screen. Joint sessions and lobby teaching can increase danger and silence disclosure. Collaterals and family maps come later, with consent, and never as the opening move while the partner waits nearby.

distractorExplanations.a: A joint genogram as the first step can put her at risk and block honest safety answers.
distractorExplanations.c: Unconsented lobby paperwork from the partner is not a safety plan and may leak her words.
distractorExplanations.d: A public lecture does not assess her risk and can escalate harm if he hears the content.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.prompt: A BSW is writing an intake on a teen in school-based services. A teacher emails unsolicited notes about the teen’s “attitude.” No parent or youth has signed a release. How should the worker treat that email?

options.a: File it as consented collateral because school staff are always on the treatment team by default
options.b: Reply asking the teacher for DSM-style diagnostic impressions to round out the mental status exam
options.c: Do not use it as authorized collateral; get a specific signed release before relying on school detail
options.d: Forward the email to child protective services because a teacher mentioned attitude problems

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.explanation: Collateral is information from other people or records the client (or guardian) authorizes. An unsolicited school email is not automatically a consented collateral. Obtain a specific release before using those details in the assessment. Attitude comments are not a mandated-report threshold by themselves.

distractorExplanations.a: School staff are not automatic collaterals; sharing still needs a specific authorization except narrow emergencies.
distractorExplanations.b: Teachers are not asked to diagnose; collateral, when authorized, is observations, not a DSM workup.
distractorExplanations.d: “Attitude” is not reasonable suspicion of abuse; dumping the email on CPS confuses collateral with a report.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.prompt: On a BSW home visit a client wears yesterday’s clothes, correctly names the date and city, and weeps while saying “I’m fine.” Which mental-status notes are appropriate without diagnosing?

options.a: Enter major depressive disorder, severe, with anxious distress on today’s problem list
options.b: Write that an SSRI is indicated and ask the physician to start a named dose this afternoon
options.c: Record suspected frontal atrophy from the tearful face and recommend a head CT this week
options.d: Note unkempt clothes, tearful affect that mismatches “I’m fine,” and intact orientation

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.explanation: A bachelor-level mental status exam records observed appearance, affect, and orientation. Incongruence between tears and “I’m fine” is useful data. It is not a DSM diagnosis, a prescription, or a radiology read. You still do not over-diagnose from a single home visit.

distractorExplanations.a: Full differential diagnosis is beyond the BSW MSE; you describe what you see, not a disorder code.
distractorExplanations.b: Prescribing is not a social-work assessment task; medication requests belong to a licensed prescriber.
distractorExplanations.c: A CT interpretation is medical; facial expression is not imaging and should not be charted as atrophy.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.prompt: A client says “sometimes I wish I wouldn’t wake up,” then smiles and changes the subject. What is the BSW’s next assessment step in this contact?

options.a: Ask directly about suicidal thoughts, plan, means, and intent before you end the contact
options.b: Have the client sign a no-suicide contract and treat the smile as proof that risk has passed
options.c: Skip further questions because a bright affect and humor mean the remark was only venting
options.d: Score only sleep, appetite, and mood on the MSE and leave suicide items for psychiatry later

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.explanation: Passive death wishes still require a direct suicide inquiry in the same contact: ideation, plan, means, and intent, then action matching the level of risk. Calm or smiling presentation does not rule out danger. No-harm contracts are not a substitute for that screen and a safety plan.

distractorExplanations.b: No-suicide contracts lack evidence as protection; they do not replace a direct risk interview.
distractorExplanations.c: People at high risk can look bright; you do not infer safety from a smile or a subject change.
distractorExplanations.d: Vegetative MSE items are not a suicide screen; ideation and plan must be asked, not deferred.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.prompt: A grandmother raising two grandchildren wants the BSW to show who is related, who lives in which household, and where cutoffs sit across generations. Which assessment tool fits that request?

options.a: An ecomap of current church, school, and agency arrows around the household this month
options.b: A genogram of kinship, households, and relationship patterns across three generations
options.c: A staff flowchart of who inside the agency signs each referral and closes each case
options.d: A job-and-housing timeline of the grandmother’s moves with no other relatives drawn

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.explanation: A genogram maps family structure, households, and relational patterns over generations. An ecomap shows present supports and stressors outside the family. Agency org charts and a one-person timeline do not answer the kinship question the grandmother asked.

distractorExplanations.a: An ecomap is the current environment, not three-generation kinship and household patterns.
distractorExplanations.c: An internal referral chart describes the agency, not the client’s family system.
distractorExplanations.d: A personal timeline omits other relatives and cutoffs, which is the point of a genogram.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.prompt: A client in crisis refuses the hospital. Relatives tell the intake BSW to “put him on a hold” before he leaves the lobby. What is the correct bachelor-level stance?

options.a: Complete the hold now because any relative’s request is enough legal authority in every state
options.b: Sign the hold yourself as the intake BSW because you saw agitation while he sat in the lobby
options.c: Treat it as a voluntary stay once he shakes his head; without his consent no statute can apply
options.d: Follow state statute and the supervisor or qualified evaluator; do not issue a solo BSW hold

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.explanation: Involuntary holds are statute-driven and typically require a qualified evaluator and supervisor consultation. Families may petition, but they cannot order a hold. A BSW does not decide a hold alone, and lack of consent is the definition of involuntary—not a reason to ignore the statute.

distractorExplanations.a: Relatives may petition; they do not themselves create hold authority by asking the BSW.
distractorExplanations.b: Lobby agitation is data for consultation, not a license for a bachelor worker to sign a hold.
distractorExplanations.c: Involuntary admission proceeds without consent under statute; refusing care does not end the duty to follow process.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.prompt: A new adult at a family-resource center smells of alcohol at 10 a.m. What is the BSW’s substance-use screening role on this intake?

options.a: Ask the agency’s standard substance questions, then refer if the screen flags concern
options.b: Order an in-house urine cup because the odor is probable cause for toxicology today
options.c: Limit screening to this client; people who look sober do not need the same questions
options.d: Chart alcohol use disorder, severe, from the odor and a missed appointment this week

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.explanation: BSW screening uses routine, standard questions (for example AUDIT or CAGE-style items) with every intake, then referral. Odor is a cue, not a diagnosis and not authority to order labs. Appearance is unreliable, so screening is not reserved for people who “look” intoxicated.

distractorExplanations.b: Toxicology is a medical order under protocol, not a BSW intake test based on smell.
distractorExplanations.c: Looking sober does not skip the screen; standardized questions are used routinely, not only when impaired.
distractorExplanations.d: Screening flags risk; a substance-use diagnosis needs a fuller qualified assessment, not odor plus a no-show.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.prompt: A man is referred for “noncompliance.” He names church, a cousin who can watch the children, and a year of stable work. The referral lists only deficits. What belongs in the BSW assessment?

options.a: Omit strengths until treatment starts; assessment should mirror the problems the court already named
options.b: Record church, kinship care, and work history as data alongside the presenting problems
options.c: Score personality-disorder traits first so listed strengths cannot mask “Axis II” pathology
options.d: Delete the problem list and keep only compliments so the record stays purely strengths-based

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.explanation: Strengths-based assessment documents resources and competencies in the same write-up as problems. Church, kinship, and work history are assessment data that shape planning. Ignoring them because a court used deficit language, or replacing problems with compliments only, both distort the picture.

distractorExplanations.a: Assessment is not a copy of the referral’s deficit list; strengths are gathered in the first evaluation.
distractorExplanations.c: Personality labeling is not the BSW task here and is not a reason to discard named supports.
distractorExplanations.d: A strengths-only file hides risk and need; problems and strengths are both recorded.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.prompt: A 9-year-old in after-school programming says Dad “hits me with the belt when I talk back” and shows a linear bruise. The parent already attends the agency’s parenting class. What should the BSW do?

options.a: Wait for photos, a police case number, and a medical note before any child-abuse report
options.b: Ask the supervisor to vote on whether a report is required this month given the bruise
options.c: Skip reporting because the family is already in services and the class counts as protection
options.d: Report to CPS on reasonable suspicion now; parenting class does not cancel the mandate

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.explanation: Mandated reporters act on reasonable suspicion, not proof. A child’s statement plus a patterned bruise meets that threshold. The duty is personal; supervisor agreement is not required, and open services do not pause reporting. Investigation belongs to CPS, not the BSW.

distractorExplanations.a: Proof, photos, and police numbers are CPS’s job; waiting for them delays a required report.
distractorExplanations.b: The mandate is the reporter’s; a supervisor cannot veto or postpone a reasonable-suspicion report.
distractorExplanations.c: Being in parenting class does not suspend the duty when new suspicion of physical abuse appears.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.prompt: A school counselor asks for a client’s whole assessment file. In the hallway the client nodded “sure.” What must the BSW have before sharing those details?

options.a: A signed, specific authorization naming what is shared, with whom, why, and when it ends
options.b: A witnessed hallway yes plus the counselor on speakerphone as a substitute for a form
options.c: An open “any records, any time” sheet so the client is not asked to sign again later
options.d: Only the BSW’s signature on letterhead stating that professional judgment supports the release

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.explanation: A valid release is written, signed, and specific: information, recipient, purpose, and expiration. A hallway nod is not an authorization. Blanket forever-releases and worker-only signatures do not meet privacy standards for assessment records.

distractorExplanations.b: Verbal or witnessed hallway consent does not replace a signed, specific authorization.
distractorExplanations.c: Blanket, open-ended releases are invalid; they must limit content, recipient, purpose, and time.
distractorExplanations.d: The client or legal representative signs; the worker’s signature is not the client’s consent.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.prompt: An intake client is tearful about “anxiety” and also has a Friday eviction notice and an empty refrigerator. What belongs in today’s BSW assessment?

options.a: Mood only; food and housing belong at the benefits office and sit outside psychosocial work
options.b: Housing, food, and benefits next to mood, because concrete needs are part of assessment
options.c: Several sessions of affect work first; concrete needs wait until anxiety looks more stable
options.d: A full GAD-versus-MDD differential before any shelter, pantry, or eviction-prevention referral

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.explanation: Person-in-environment assessment includes food, housing, and benefits with emotional presentation. Concrete scarcity often drives distress, so it is assessed and addressed early. Bachelor practice does not wait for a DSM differential before linking someone to shelter or food.

distractorExplanations.a: Concrete needs are core to psychosocial assessment, not an errand left only to a benefits clerk.
distractorExplanations.c: Waiting for mood to “stabilize” before housing inverts the usual order when eviction is days away.
distractorExplanations.d: Diagnosis is not the BSW prerequisite for resource linkage; safety and basic needs are assessed now.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.prompt: A 78-year-old misses two of three Mini-Cog words and places clock numbers poorly. An adult child says “put dementia in the chart.” What should the BSW record?

options.a: Alzheimer’s disease as established, because a failed Mini-Cog is treated as diagnostic
options.b: A completed neuropsychological battery, so no further cognitive testing is needed
options.c: A positive screen only, with limits explained, and a referral for medical evaluation
options.d: Lack of legal capacity for finances, based on the clock drawing as a capacity test

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.explanation: Mini-Cog and clock-draw are brief screens, not a dementia diagnosis, a neuropsych battery, or a capacity finding. The BSW documents the screen, explains that it only flags possible impairment, and refers for medical or fuller cognitive evaluation.

distractorExplanations.a: Alzheimer’s requires medical workup; a screening miss is not a diagnosis you enter as fact.
distractorExplanations.b: A three-minute screen is not hours of standardized neuropsychology and does not close the workup.
distractorExplanations.d: Decisional capacity is a separate determination; a poor clock does not settle legal finances.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.prompt: An elder prefers Mixtec. Her adult son offers to interpret “so we can go faster,” including questions about whether anyone at home mistreats her. What should the BSW do?

options.a: Use the son, because family interpreters are more culturally accurate than vendor interpreters
options.b: Interview in slow English only and skip an interpreter so household details stay in the room
options.c: Put the mistreatment questions into a phone app and continue without a human interpreter
options.d: Get a qualified interpreter; do not use the son for assessment, especially abuse content

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.explanation: Cultural humility in assessment means meaningful language access through a qualified interpreter, not assuming family can speak for the elder. Relatives, especially possible caregivers, introduce error, bias, and confidentiality risk on abuse items. Apps and slow English do not replace that access.

distractorExplanations.a: Family interpreters are a cultural-humility miss when they may be the alleged harm source or filter.
distractorExplanations.b: Slow English does not create access; it also does not protect her if she cannot report harm in English.
distractorExplanations.c: Translation apps are inaccurate and not confidential enough for clinical or abuse assessment.

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.prompt: The BSW is writing the assessment summary for case planning. Which problem statement fits bachelor-level practice?

options.a: Client meets DSM-5-TR criteria for 300.02 generalized anxiety disorder as the case problem
options.b: Underlying enmeshment and poor object relations are the true drivers of this week’s crisis
options.c: Client wants help stopping Friday evictions and says, “I need a lock that actually works”
options.d: Improve well-being and insight over the next six months as tolerated, per worker formulation

aswb-bachelors-readiness-check-assessmen.explanation: A bachelor-level problem statement is specific, observable, and close to the client’s words plus context. A DSM code, a psychodynamic root-cause claim, or a vague well-being goal is not that statement. Planning starts from the eviction and the lock the client named.

distractorExplanations.a: A diagnosis code is a label, not a BSW problem statement in the client’s observable terms.
distractorExplanations.b: Root-cause interpretation is the worker’s hypothesis, not the shared, observable problem statement.
distractorExplanations.d: A broad well-being goal confuses the problem with a vague outcome and drops the concrete concern.
